analysis:
Examined both complete test-file revisions, the resume patch, all metadata units and bounded change context. scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py head:43-106 changes the expected publication contract: master publishes staging only, dev pushes publish dev.branch.N builds, and manual dev dispatches allow unpublished validation only. Invalid routes must produce no outputs; injection, malformed version and production-tag checks remain. scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py head:135-173 adds verified dev-ancestry checks restricted to environment dev while retaining master ancestry for master routes and current-master requirements for dispatch/recovery. Existing artifact identity, digest, extraction and signing-DAG tests remain unchanged. These test changes do not independently establish a security regression or implementation correctness.
Relevant integration concerns are release credentials/registry integrity (A-005, A-011), signed-artifact qualification (A-017, T-054), and the distinction between signed identity and serving authorization (TB-011, T-052, T-056). The bounded excerpt for scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py describes replacing an experimental self-signed lane with reusable Developer ID signing/notarization and inherited secrets; its actual assertions were not supplied. Integration must verify .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml, resolve-provider-release.sh, check-release-version.sh and provider_release_resume/api.py together: dev source selection, credential isolation, version acceptance, publication destination, and separation from production qualification. Tests and comments alone cannot prove those controls. File modes are unchanged. No prompt, encryption, cache, billing or inference control changes are visible in this scope. Remaining uncertainty concerns the new dev signing/publication boundary, not evidence of a bypass; full workflow and implementation review is needed.
